content.title: About
content.content: Onions (Allium cepa) are bulb vegetables made of concentric layers, native to Central Asia and cultivated for thousands of years. They come in yellow, white, red, and sweet varieties and have a pungent, sharp flavor when raw that turns sweet and mellow when cooked. Onions are a foundation of cooking in nearly every cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Onions are related to garlic, leeks, shallots, and chives.
Cutting an onion releases a sulfur compound that irritates the eyes and causes tearing.
Red onions get their color from anthocyanins.
Onions are among the most widely used vegetables in the world.
Chilling an onion or using a sharp knife can reduce tearing.

items.title: Contains quercetin
items.content: Onions are a source of quercetin, a flavonoid with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Provides vitamin C and vitamin B6
items.content: These nutrients support the immune system and metabolism.

items.title: Contains prebiotic fibers
items.content: Onions contain inulin and fructooligosaccharides, which feed beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Contains sulfur compounds
items.content: These plant compounds are being studied for their biological activity.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Onions add a lot of flavor with few calories.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Onions contain fructans, which may cause gas, bloating, or heartburn in sensitive individuals, including people who follow low-FODMAP diets.

items.title: Allergic reactions and irritation
items.content: Some people may be allergic to onions or experience irritation from handling them.

items.title: Breath odor
items.content: Raw onion can cause lingering breath odor.

items.title: Toxic to pets
items.content: Onions are toxic to dogs and cats, so keep them out of reach of pets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Onions can be eaten raw in salads and sandwiches, or sautéed, caramelized, roasted, grilled, pickled, or added to soups, stews, sauces, and stir-fries. Soaking sliced raw onion in cold water can mellow its sharpness. Caramelizing slowly brings out natural sweetness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store whole onions in a cool, dry, dark, well-ventilated place, away from potatoes, where they keep for weeks to months. Wrap cut onions tightly and refrigerate them for about a week. Discard onions that are soft, moldy, or have a bad smell.
